When a tuning system is active, the first resonator is tuned to an absolute pitch defined by the tuning, while the remaining resonators are tuned relative to its pitch.

The Note parameter sets the root pitch of all the resonators. By default, the pitch is set in semitones ranging from C-1 to C5. When scale awareness is enabled, the pitch is set in scale degrees. When a tuning system is active, the pitch is set in note indices based on the tuning system’s set of pitches. You can make fine adjustments in cents using the Resonator I Fine Tuning parameter.

Resonators II through V follow the Note parameter defined in Resonator I, but they can each be individually transposed by ±24 semitones or ±21 scale degrees (if the effect is scale aware) using their individual Pitch controls. Additional fine tuning is available through the Resonator II–V Fine Tuning parameters.

source_references.quote: The Stereo control determines the width of the output’s stereo image. At the highest setting of 120 degrees, each ear receives a reverberant channel that is independent of the other (this is also a property of the diffusion in real rooms). The lowest setting mixes the output signal to mono.
The Density chooser controls the tradeoff between reverb quality and performance. Sparse uses minimal CPU resources, while High delivers the richest reverberation.
At the reverb output, you can vary the amplitude of reflections and diffusion with the Reflect and Diffuse controls and adjust the effect’s overall Dry/Wet mix.
